build: cmake + g++ 14, C++17, Release, header-only targets
configure_note: LibTorch targets (odfm_runner, odfm_parity_check) did NOT build. The installed torch wheel is a CUDA build (2.13.0+cu130) and its Caffe2Config.cmake refuses to configure without CUDA present. The header-only runtime primitives and their tests have no such dependency and build anywhere, which is the point of that split in CMakeLists.txt.

tests.flakiness: test_spsc_ring failed once during a -j4 parallel build, then passed 40/40 when run alone. That points at CPU contention in a timing-sensitive concurrency test rather than a logic defect, but a test that fails only under load is exactly the kind CI hides.

benchmark.what: Producer/consumer handoff through the SPSC ring with the latency accumulator, no model in the loop -- the floor the runtime imposes.
benchmark.note: Throughput is bounded by the producer's deliberate 50 us pacing, not by the ring. Queueing latency is the number that matters: 300 ns at the median, 7.8 us at p99.

hardware: cloud container CPU, 4 cores, g++ -O2, no -march=native (CMakeLists deliberately leaves it off so numbers stay reproducible)
